introduction:
The 'Formwork for Concrete Structures- Virtual Laboratory' provides students with practical exposure to different formwork systems used in reinforced concrete construction. Through interactive virtual experiments, students can understand the components, assembly sequence, construction procedure, and application of formwork for foundations, walls, columns, beams, and slabs.

The laboratory covers both conventional and modern formwork systems, including simple formwork, climbing formwork, PERI systems, Flex formwork, heavy-duty (HD) tower systems, and aluminium formwork. The virtual format enables students to learn and practise important construction procedures remotely, without requiring continuous access to a physical construction laboratory or site.

UG: The laboratory is primarily intended for undergraduate students of Civil Engineering and Construction Engineering & Management. It can also be useful for diploma students, faculty members, site engineers, and young construction professionals who want a basic practical understanding of formwork systems. Because the experiments are virtual and presented in a relatively simple manner, they can also serve as a pre-laboratory or pre-site-visit learning tool, allowing students to understand the basic components and construction sequence before handling actualformwork.

objective:
The laboratory aims to provide students with an accessible and practical virtual learning environment for understanding the components, assembly, construction sequence, and application of conventional and modern formwork systems used in concrete construction.

The main objectives of these virtual experiments are to:
  • Familiarize students with different types of formwork systems and their components.
  • Demonstrate the step-by-step assembly and construction sequence of formwork for foundations, walls, columns, beams, and slabs.
  • Help students understand the differences between conventional and proprietary/modern formwork systems.
  • Introduce students to systems such as PERI, climbing formwork, Flex formwork, HD towers, and aluminium formwork.
  • Develop an understanding of how the appropriate formwork system is selected for different structural elements and construction situations.
  • Provide students with practical construction exposure through a virtual environment, particularly when access to physical formwork systems or construction sites is limited.


These objectives are consistent with formwork education more broadly, which emphasizes conventional and proprietary formwork, erection, safety, applications, and problem-solving skills.

universities: The virtual laboratory is most directly aligned with courses such as: Formwork for Concrete Structures, Building Construction, Construction Technology, Construction Methods and Equipment, Concrete Construction, and Construction Engineering and Management.
At IIT Delhi, Formwork for Concrete Structures is itself offered as a Civil Engineering course, demonstrating the direct academic relevance of this virtual laboratory.

The experiments can complement classroom teaching by providing the practical/visual component of topics taught theoretically. For example, after learning about wall or slab formwork in a lecture, students can use the corresponding virtual experiment to understand how the system is assembled and used in practice.
